title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25). The preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible deterministically from the archived per‑pair raw_results (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using the preregistered seed (1729) and 10,000 resamples; we provide a compact reproduction recipe and an explicit per‑repair provenance mapping in the text. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide explicit artifact pointers and checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) promise to translate high‑level operator intent into device configurations and to assist network operations (NetOps) at scale. Operational NetOps requires not only syntactic plausibility but demonstrable functional correctness, bounded blast radius (limited collateral impact), and auditability. A widely proposed architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM generates a candidate configuration; a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants and policy constraints; an automated repair subroutine attempts to correct violations (possibly iteratively). Prior tool‑assisted critique and verifier literature (e.g., CRITIC) motivates such pipelines but there is limited preregistered within‑task paired evidence isolating the verifier effect with full provenance. We therefore ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) and executed it end‑to‑end with archival of inputs, outputs, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: Prior work on LLM→IaC and intent translation (PreConfig, intent engines, intent translation papers) demonstrates the feasibility of LLM‑based configuration proposals but highlights correctness and safety gaps. Work on tool‑assisted critiquing and self‑correction (CRITIC, tool‑interactive critiquing) suggests verifiers can reduce semantic errors. Deterministic NetOps verifiers and ensemble verification (SymNet, ensemble verification approaches) provide foundations for fast functional checks. Recent surveys of LLMs for NetOps and intent engines document architectural desiderata (auditability, verifier coverage, repair budgets) and report ceiling effects when baseline model correctness is already high. Our study contributes a preregistered within‑task paired evaluation that isolates the verifier’s causal effect with full artifact release, explicit accounting of repair invocations, and reproducible analysis artifacts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified a paired confirmatory design. Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline) on a per‑task deterministic functional correctness indicator emitted by a deterministic validator. Primary hypothesis H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (power ≈ 80% with 200 pairs under the preregistered discordant assumption). Task generation and inclusion rules. We generated 200 stratified tasks with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 constrained to features covered by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Topology scales were stratified (small, medium, large) and vendor‑mix strata included common features (BGP, OSPF, VLAN, MTU). Tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were detected and excluded automatically (deterministic inclusion/exclusion logged; task manifest SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Execution adapter and model. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed paired episodes using the declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Per the preregistration, each task used a single shared initial generation (shared candidate reused across guarded and baseline conditions). Guarded condition semantics. Guarded episodes first invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5; when violations were flagged the pipeline invoked an automated repair subroutine once (preregistered maximum = 1). The verifier emitted structured traces (validation_before/validation_after) that include parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count and validation final_state; these per‑episode validator traces are archived in execution/scoring/*.json (example hashes provided in the Disclosure). Analysis plan and reproducibility. Primary test: exact two‑sided McNemar on complete pairs with 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Missingness policy: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed) with a prespecified sensitivity 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat both‑missing pairs as failures). All raw per‑episode records, seeds, prompts, provider calls, validator traces and execution logs were archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7). Analysis executor identifier: paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis artifacts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766).
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2). Completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs included in the primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (recorded in analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Primary confirmatory (complete pairs n = 188). Contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e...): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both fail within complete pairs). Aggregate: baseline_success = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_success = 188/188 = 1.0; Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl documents seed and resample count; artifact SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc). Sensitivity (both_missing → failures). Following the preregistered sensitivity, include all 200 pairs, yielding n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12, guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Reproducible bootstrap CI for the sensitivity. The preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis was computed by resampling the full set of 200 archived per‑pair records in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) with replacement 10,000 times using seed=1729 and recomputing Δ per resample; the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles yield the bootstrap CI reported in the archive. The analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records the bootstrap parameters and the paired_binary_analysis_v1 invocation; reproducing this CI is deterministic from the archived raw per‑pair records (recipe in Reproducibility section). Repair mapping and provenance (reviewer request). The execution archive links each repair invocation to explicit provider_call filenames and SHA‑256 checksums inside the provider_calls directory; the three repair invocations correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). For deterministic verification we include here the minimal deterministic linkage extracted from execution/raw_results.jsonl (artifact SHA‑256 above). The paper lists the per‑repair mapping as a compact archival table (Table 1) showing episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/) and provider_call_sha256 and final_score. Table 1 entries are extracted verbatim from execution/raw_results.jsonl and from the provider_calls directory; the full per‑call provider traces and their SHA‑256s are present in the supplied artifact bundle and are recoverable using the checksums reported in the Disclosure Statement. Representative per‑episode validator traces. Representative scoring JSONs included in the archive (e.g., execution/scoring/task‑000001‑guarded.json SHA‑256 = 60f5b7a7..., task‑000002‑guarded.json SHA‑256 = 9d60eda6..., task‑000003‑guarded.json SHA‑256 = 2ff9540d...) show structured validator traces (validation_before/validation_after) with parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count; these traces substantiate the reported per‑episode success indicators and provide the per‑episode blast‑radius diagnostics used in exploratory reporting. Repair activity and blast radius. Repair invocations were rare (3); each successful repair reduced a failing shared initial candidate into a validator‑passing final configuration in the guarded condition (n_10 = 3). The verifier traces contain observed_touched_field_count and parsed_command_count which are the available per‑episode, artifact‑grounded blast‑radius diagnostics; aggregate blast‑radius statistics were not computed as preregistered exploratory estimands because repair invocations were too few for robust inference, but the per‑episode validator traces are archived for follow‑up analyses.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement in success rate (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes corrected by the automated repair path. The effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and is not statistically significant at alpha = 0.05. Two operational causes are evident in the archived artifacts: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and selection — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and the sampled synthetic task family produced many LLM proposals that already matched the golden configuration or passed validation, so repairs were rarely invoked (repair stage invocations = 3). Implications for NetOps practice. Deterministic verifiers add auditability and can correct some LLM mistakes, but measurable operational benefit requires (a) a nontrivial baseline error floor where LLMs make fixable functional mistakes; (b) verifier coverage aligned with the likely error patterns; and (c) an adequate repair budget (multiple iterations) to address complex violations. For high‑baseline correctness settings, verifier utility may be primarily in confidence and audit trails rather than large absolute improvements in success rate. Reproducibility and reviewer‑requested artifacts. To address reviewer requirements we provide exact reproduction instructions for the preregistered bootstrap CIs and an explicit per‑repair provenance mapping. Reproducing the bootstrap CI (complete pair or sensitivity): 1) load execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7), 2) extract per‑pair binary outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) for the desired missingness treatment, 3) with seed=1729 draw 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the pairs (sample indices with replacement), compute Δ per resample, and take the 2.5th/97.5th percentiles. The analysis/analysis_log.jsonl documents the exact seed and resample count used by paired_binary_analysis_v1 (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a...). Per‑repair provenance mapping (Table 1). Table 1 in this manuscript is a compact, archival‑derived table copied deterministically from execution/raw_results.jsonl and the provider_calls directory. It lists the three repair invocations with episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative path under execution/provider_calls/), provider_call_sha256, and final_score. These entries are present verbatim in the supplied evidence bundle and can be cross‑checked using the raw_results.jsonl checksum above. Threats to validity. Internal validity: single shared initial candidate per pair (preregistered), limited retries, and 24 failed episodes reduced the analytic complete_pair set to 188. Construct validity: the success metric is a deterministic validator‑based functional correctness indicator and depends on verifier coverage and the fidelity of synthetic golden configs. External validity: single‑model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic Cornetto‑like tasks, and the limited verifier scope restrict generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) limit power to detect effects smaller than the preregistered 20‑pp threshold. Recommendations. Future studies should (a) increase baseline task difficulty or include tasks outside current verifier coverage to raise LLM error rates; (b) increase repair budgets (multiple automated iterations) and log iterative traces; (c) evaluate multiple LLM families and verifiers; (d) compute and report per‑call blast‑radius distributions (observed_touched_field_count) when repair counts permit robust inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; however high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, model ensembles, and repair budgets.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Models & provider: all generation calls used declared model gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd. Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in Dockerized environments; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 preregistration SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3 was archived prior to observing final execution outputs. Initial master prompt reference (immutable archived path): provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution & analysis provenance: the execution manifest and analysis artifacts record all prompts, raw outputs, verifier traces, parsed IRs, seeds, and hashes. Key artifact pointers and checksums (relative paths inside the supplied manuscript evidence bundle): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipe (bootstrap CI and sensitivity). To reproduce the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI (complete pair or sensitivity): 1) load execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above), 2) extract per‑pair binary outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) according to the preregistered missingness policy (complete_pair_primary or the sensitivity that treats both‑missing pairs as failures), 3) with seed=1729 draw 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the pairs (indices sampled with replacement), compute Δ per resample, and take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records the exact seed and resample count used by paired_binary_analysis_v1. Per‑repair provenance mapping. The three repair invocations that yielded the three guarded‑only successes are recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the provider_calls directory; execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) links each repair invocation to episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/), provider_call_sha256, and final_score. The paper provides a compact archival Table 1 copied verbatim from those archived records for deterministic verification; readers can cross‑check the provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s against the provider_calls directory in the published artifact bundle. Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 but was not recomputed inline in the printed manuscript because the drafting snapshot did not contain a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the supplied snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the above checksum.
